title: The Flour

where.detail: at his cot in the infirmary hall, the kitchen novice still kneeling over the flour at the undercroft door

time: the dawn bell and the hour after it, the morning after the eve
last_beat: "Then ask her faster, Captain," he said. "He's not getting any warmer."

people.did: Read the flour at the undercroft door at the dawn bell; held the House to the Mender's count and the Prior's key and sent the eager ones to carry wood up the bell tower; asked Maelis again, and gave her the answer to the Prior's question: he will come back up, on this leg.
people.now: At his cot in the hall. The House knows the cold comes up every night through the gap under the undercroft door, and is held to the Mender's count and the Prior's key. Maelis has told him his answer is the right one and not true yet: ask tomorrow.

facts.fact: He read the flour by a lamp held low on the flags: no print in it or out, but a half-moon of frost glazed into it from the gap, every grain leaning toward the door.
facts.evidence: every grain of that glaze caught the light the same way, all of them leaning, as if the floor had been combed toward the door in the night

facts.fact: He believes something on the other side draws on the hall through the gap; the novice said breathed on, he said breathed in.
facts.evidence: "Breathed in," Darrow said.

facts.fact: He sent the lay brother from the fire and the young ones with the mallet to carry wood up the bell tower for Sister Pell instead.
facts.evidence: If you want something to carry, carry that.

facts.fact: Told he would want to be first down, he said he would be, on the Mender's count and with the Prior's key, and the last to arrive.
facts.evidence: On the Mender's count, with the Prior's key. I'll just be the last to arrive.

facts.fact: He would not let the House take the undercroft door off its pins: the Prior has the key, and the Mender has his word.
facts.evidence: Nobody touches this door without the Prior. She has the key, and the Mender has my word.

facts.fact: Asked by Maelis what he will do at the bottom of the stair, he said he will come back up, on this leg.
facts.evidence: He put his hand on the knee, the way you put a hand on a horse you are about to ask something of.

people.did: Rang the hours through the night and came down between every bell to sit by the undercroft door; heard nothing come or go; told Hollis she would sleep after the noon bell.
people.now: Gone up to her bell tower after the dawn bell, her palms raw from the rope; the lay brothers are carrying wood up to her.

facts.fact: She climbed the bell tower and came back down to sit by the undercroft door eight times between the night bell and the dawn bell.
facts.evidence: Up the tower. Ring. Down the stair. Sit. Up again. Eight times.

facts.fact: Nothing came through the undercroft door or went in that night, by her ear.
facts.evidence: Nothing came through that door, Captain, and nothing went in.

facts.fact: Her palms are rubbed red by the rope in two straight lines.
facts.evidence: they were red across the palms in two straight lines

people.did: Read the knee at the hour; when the Captain asked again, asked him first what he will do at the bottom; told him 'come back up, on this' is the right answer and not true yet, and to ask tomorrow; went to the far cots without a lamp.
people.now: At the far cots. She has told the Captain his answer is right and not yet true, and to ask her again tomorrow.

facts.fact: Asked again, she asked him first what he will do at the bottom of the stair.
facts.evidence: Then I'll ask you something first. What will you do at the bottom?

facts.fact: She told him his answer, to come back up on this leg, is the right one and is not true yet, and to ask her tomorrow.
facts.evidence: That's the right answer," she said. "It isn't true yet. Ask me tomorrow.

people.did: Counted the flour: no prints in or out, frost; said the seam on the wall sweats every dawn she has looked; showed the Captain a fresh ledger page counting the times he has asked the Mender, and added to it.
people.now: With her ledger, keeping the count of the times the Captain has asked the Mender.

facts.fact: She counted no prints into the flour and none out, and frost.
facts.evidence: "Prints in," she said. "None. Prints out. None. Frost."

facts.fact: She says the seam on the wall sweats every dawn she has looked, so this is not new: only the first night anyone sat up with it.
facts.evidence: It's not new. It's just the first night anyone sat up with it.

facts.fact: She has started a ledger page counting the times the Captain has asked the Mender, with a great deal of room under it.
facts.evidence: Times the Captain has asked the Mender: 1.

people.did: At the Grey Cot with the lad's hand; told Sister Pell to go and get some sleep, heard himself, and closed his hand on the lad's; told the Captain, who had been told not yet, to ask her faster.
people.now: At the Grey Cot with the lad's hand, waiting on the Mender's yes.

facts.fact: He told Sister Pell to go and get some sleep, the same words he had given the lad the last night the lad could hear them, and his hand closed slowly on the lad's.
facts.evidence: the same words he had given the lad, the last night the lad could hear them

facts.fact: Told the Mender has not said yes yet, he told the Captain to ask her faster, because the lad is not getting any warmer.
facts.evidence: Then ask her faster, Captain

fired.evidence: "Go and get some sleep, sister," he said. "The door'll keep."

now.against: Something below the hall draws on it every night through the gap under the undercroft door; the stair waits on the Mender's yes, and the leg is not ready.
now.next: Asking Maelis again, until the leg will bear him on a stair.

title: Even Money

where.detail: in the kitchen after the night bell, at the bread table with the kitchen's book

time: after the night bell, the day after the eve
last_beat: The novice wrote that down too, because the kitchen wrote everything down, and Rae went back to her halter as if nothing had been owed in the first place.

people.did: Went to the kitchen after the night bell; would not let the novice rub out the prices because NOBODY has not won yet, and gave her the nights to cross off instead; gave Rae the aye he owed her.
people.now: In the kitchen after the night bell. He owes Rae a plain telling of what the cold does on the stone, once he has been down the stair.

facts.fact: He told the kitchen novice the bet on NOBODY is that no other cot goes grey before the thaw, not who did it, and that nobody has won anything yet.
facts.evidence: The bet was no other cot goes grey before the thaw," he said. "Not who did it.

facts.fact: He told her to cross off a night every dawn there is no new grey blanket.
facts.evidence: Every dawn there's no new grey blanket, put a line through one.

facts.fact: He gave Rae the aye he lost to her on the gate wall: when he has been down the stair he will tell her what the cold does on the stone, plainly.
facts.evidence: When you've been down that stair, you'll tell me what the cold does on the stone. Plain. Not how you'd tell the House.

people.did: Sat splicing a halter on the kitchen's second bench; read the book like a load (the whole House is under it now); claimed the aye the Captain owes her.
people.now: In the kitchen at night, splicing a halter. The Captain owes her a plain telling of what the cold does on the stone below the House.

facts.fact: She read the kitchen's book like a load and said the whole House is under it now.
facts.evidence: Heavy book," she said. "Whole House is under it now.

facts.fact: She claimed her aye: when the Captain has been down the stair he is to tell her what the cold does on the stone, plain, not how he would tell the House.
facts.evidence: I'll have my aye.

codex.name: Nights without
codex.text: A margin the kitchen novice keeps in the kitchen's betting book since the Captain would not let NOBODY be paid out: a stroke for every dawn with no new grey blanket in the hall (Ch 3, Between).

now.against: Something below the hall draws on it every night; the House has bet on nobody, and the thaw is a long way off.
now.next: The stair, on the Mender's count.
